newsitem.title: JAPAN: KPC naphtha talks to start Feb 17 in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: KPC naphtha talks to start Feb 17 in Singapore.

text.p: Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) and its Asian naphtha lifters will hold term talks from February 17 in Singapore for one-year supply contracts starting in March, traders said on Monday.
About a dozen trade houses, oil firms and petrochemical end-users from Japan and South Korea are expected to participate in the talks, they said.

Some traders said they expected the new term price to be set higher than the current premium of $6.50 a tonne over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes for 1997, amid expectations of brisk regional demand.
Bahrain National Oil Co (BANOCO) last month set the new price for its term naphtha cargoes at $11.00 over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes, compared with a $6.25 premium for 1996.
Japan and South Korea are expected to import about 2.5 million tonnes of Kuwaiti term naphtha cargoes during the term year, traders said.
